Frequently Asked Questions # HerMin publishes application-specific FAQs on its official pages. The answers below consolidate the recurring questions about MOQs, lead times, production, certifications, technologies and customization. Full original answers are available on the official application pages linked at the end.
Orders and MOQs # What are the minimum order quantities for custom fabrics and garment manufacturing? The standard fabric MOQ is 1,000 yards per color / 3,000 yards per order. Smaller test runs are possible with a small-lot surcharge. For garment manufacturing (FOB), the MOQ starts at 300 pieces per style. Underwear garment MOQ is 1,000 pieces per style with a nominal surcharge, and finished accessories can start at 100 pieces per style.
Why is the underwear garment MOQ higher than streetwear? A pair of underwear uses very little fabric. To consume a minimum viable production run of fabric, a higher number of garment units is required. HerMin’s 1,000-piece MOQ is still far below the 5,000–10,000 piece standard common in the industry.
Can HerMin handle large orders? Yes. HerMin describes turnkey management for complex 10,000+ unit supply chains and cites a 10,000+ piece fitness chain uniform program in its portfolio.
Lead Times # What is the average lead time from sampling to bulk production? Assuming base yarns are in stock, fabric sampling takes about 40–45 days and bulk fabric production 60–70 days. For garments, sampling takes around 30 days and bulk production 50–60 days. HerMin recommends starting seasonal development at least 6 months in advance.
What is the lead time for accessories? Fabric sampling takes 30–45 days and bulk fabric production around 60 days. Finished accessory production, including sampling and manufacturing, typically takes 60–90 days. A 4–6 month development window is recommended.
Production Locations # Where are HerMin’s fabrics and garments produced? 100% of fabric R&D and production takes place in Taiwan. For garments, HerMin recommends boutique orders (under 1,000 pieces) locally in Taiwan. For larger volume orders, it partners with certified overseas garment factories with long-standing relationships.
Does HerMin produce hard-shell jackets with seam taping? Taiwanese garment lines rarely have seam-taping equipment, making local production expensive. If a hard-shell project reaches at least 3,000 pieces per style, HerMin can manage production through specialized overseas factory partners equipped for high-volume seam-taped manufacturing.
Certifications and Testing # Are HerMin’s eco-friendly fabrics certified? HerMin displays OEKO-TEX Standard 100, Global Recycled Standard (GRS), Higg Index, Organic Content Standard (OCS) and GOTS certificates. The company states its products are made in Taiwan with GOTS 6.0 and OEKO-TEX 100, and that it is GRS certified for recycled programs.
Can HerMin provide functional and physical testing reports? Yes. HerMin operates an in-house physical and chemical testing laboratory and can test water penetration, moisture vapor permeability, shrinkage, colorfastness and tensile strength during development and bulk production. For official third-party reports from agencies such as ITS or SGS, HerMin can facilitate submission; third-party testing fees are billed separately.
How durable is the PFC-free (C0) water-repellent treatment after washing? For natural staple fibers such as cotton, linen, wool and silk, the standard rating is 90/100 before washing and 70–80 after 5 washes. For synthetic filament fibers such as nylon and polyester, the standard rating is 90/100 before washing and 70–80 after up to 20 washes.
Fabric Technologies # How does BNS™ Bouncy Technology achieve stretch without spandex? BNS™ is a proprietary pre-dye and after-dye treatment that structurally enhances 100% cotton yarns to create natural mechanical stretch. Because there is no synthetic elastane to degrade, the fabric maintains breathability, smoothness and shape after repeated washing.
Will UMORFIL® Bionic Collagen properties wash out? No. UMORFIL® integrates ocean-sourced collagen peptides into the molecular structure of the nylon fiber itself rather than applying a surface coating, so the skin-soothing and deodorizing properties are designed to last the life of the garment.
How does HerMin ensure sizing consistency for high-stretch leggings? HerMin monitors stretch modulus and shrinkage rates for every batch in its in-house laboratory. Precise heat-setting helps ensure bulk fabric tension and dimensions match the approved sample.
Can specific performance finishes be added to custom fabrics? Yes. HerMin can add moisture-wicking, contact-cooling, durable antimicrobial/anti-odor, PFC-free DWR and other finishes without compromising the fabric’s handfeel.
Custom Development # How do we initiate a new development project? For fabric development, send a physical swatch for structural and composition analysis. For garment development, provide design sketches, Tech Packs or measurement charts, plus reference samples if available. This helps HerMin provide an accurate assessment and quotation.
Can HerMin develop a unique silhouette rather than using standard shapes? Yes. HerMin has in-house pattern makers and sample developers experienced in close-to-body garments, streetwear and functional apparel. The team can reverse-engineer or custom-draft patterns from a Tech Pack, sketch or reference sample.
Can HerMin match brand colors consistently across reorders? For bulk orders, HerMin implements a color tolerance policy of Delta E < 1 and maintains digital color profiles with spectrophotometer readings to keep reorders consistent with the original batch.
Can HerMin produce custom-branded waistbands for underwear? Yes. HerMin can help source and develop custom waistbands, including branded jacquard elastics, designed to be soft against the skin and retain elasticity.
Accessories # Does HerMin offer natural waxing options? Yes. HerMin offers premium beeswax imported from Germany and plant-based wax options. These natural waxes provide water repellency and develop a patina over time.
Why is PET-coated recycled polyester described as 100% recyclable? The construction is mono-material: recycled polyester base fabric plus a PET coating with identical chemical properties. This avoids mixed-material waste and allows the product to re-enter existing recycling systems after use.
What types of headwear does HerMin produce? HerMin produces 5-panel camp caps, bucket hats and unstructured dad hats. When paired with anti-UV or moisture-wicking performance fabrics, the headwear offers functional protection and comfort.

From Natural to Functional # HerMin applies bionic principles to recreate natural features in textiles. These four innovation platforms show how the company combines natural fibers with weaving, yarn and finishing technologies to replace synthetic performance materials.
BNS Bouncy™ Technology # BNS Bouncy™ Technology allows natural fibers such as cotton, Tencel®, Modal®, linen and MMCFs to stretch without elastane, Lycra® or spandex. The result is a 100% biodegradable bouncy fabric that feels soft, stretches naturally and performs well.
100% biodegradable and made with natural fibers. Natural stretch without synthetic elastic fibers. Woven and knit applicable: single jersey, French terry, diamond pique, interlock, fleece, rib, poplin, dobby and twill. Ideal for: polo shirts, underwear, yoga wear, shirting and pants. Certifications: made in Taiwan with GOTS 6.0 and OEKO-TEX 100. Weatherpoof Cotton / Tencel® # Weatherpoof Cotton is a waterproof cotton fabric made from extra-thin, long-staple cotton fibers using a very tight traditional weave. When dry, the fabric opens its pores to breathe. When wet, the over-tightened cotton fibers swell and seal the weave, making it waterproof.
Available from 200 to 286 g/sm, positioned as an alternative to hardshell synthetic fabrics. PFC-free and GOTS-certified organic cotton options are available. Characteristics: water repellent, durable water resistance, breathable, sustainable and windproof. Test data shown by HerMin: Rain Test AATCC 35 below 1 g; Bundesmann Test ISO 9865 rating 4. Wind Resistance Cotton / Tencel® # Wind Resistance Cotton is manufactured from thousands of thin cotton fibers with special weaving techniques. Based on the principles of geological compaction, the weave is durably compacted using pressure and temperature, giving the material its characteristic glossy appearance. No coating is applied.
Available in cotton and Tencel in a ripstop weave, between 90 and 100 gsm. A natural alternative to lightweight synthetic fabrics. GOTS-certified organic cotton options are available. Characteristics: windproof, water repellent, water resistant, sustainable and breathable. Bio Softshell # Bio Softshell is a fleece fabric crafted from 100% cotton and natural fibers, setting it apart from conventional synthetic fleece. HerMin’s finishing process creates no microplastics, and the fabric is 100% biodegradable.
Water repellent, thermal, breathable and naturally stretchable. 100% mono-component, biodegradable and sustainable. Available as woven softshell and knit softshell.
